comments.value:
The main draw for VRchat for me, is that I can be a giant, or macro.  In almost every roleplay environment I often portray myself as a gigantic character, even in text-only RP.  The fact VRchat allowed me to create a character of great size, even if I had to do a work around, has been the biggest draw for me.  If that were to be lost, I would quickly lose interest.  I know I have been a big influence for some folks who see my avatar and suddenly want to be big too... and I feel guilty for being one of the reasons why c.c...

However I think it should remain something you can't just do right away, but with some know-how, can still be done.  One of the reasons I like how it is in Second Life, it actually takes some work to get an avatar to be not only be big... but actually look good too!  (animations in second life don't scale up, so you need custom animations that do)

Granted, it is a bit easier to bypass the limit in VRC, but still a barrier that limits any random person from uploading a giant from the get go.  I wouldn't mind if it were a little harder, or you needed special permissions from developers to be allowed, but still not outright banned.  

I personally think though, we already have means of disabling avatars, I just think instead of having Block and Mute, there be a 3rd option, that sets that player to a standard avatar, like how Panic mode works, instead of turning everyone over a threshhold (I hated when Second Life added that in.)

Having a marker over the head, like how mute does, like an eyeball, that'd be fine.

details:
Throughout my many hours on VRChat, I've seen quite a few bizarre avatars. The avatars that generally entertain me the most are ones that use massive models, particles, and sound effects that take up the entire map. Sometimes they are creative and other times they are stupid, but either way, they show how far some people are willing to go to get the most attention possible.

However, in some updates to the SDK, avatars that were possible to create in the past are no longer allowed with the new limitations. Don't get me wrong, I understand completely why these exist; The problem is that some users are trying to get the old SDKs working so they can continue making huge avatars and stuff like that. I feel that with so many people trying to do it this way, putting limitations wasn't an entirely effective way to tone down the creation and usage of massive avatars.

With all that said, I have an idea that might allow the creation of these avatars without disruption.

My thought is if there is an option to disable the viewing of avatars altogether, why not have an option that disables the viewing of avatars over a certain poly count or size, maybe even a slider for how far you can hear sound effects? This way, people who want to see their friends' avatars don't have to be disrupted by massive avatars that lag or disrupt their game!

With these options available, limitations can be removed from the SDK (not including the 20,000 poly limit) and instead be in the hands of the user who wants or does not want to see the avatars in-game. People who have these options enabled/disabled could have markers over their head like the other options, just to let the massive avatar users know how much attention they are actually getting.

I hope this idea will be helpful for allowing creativity or stupidity to thrive within VRChat without being an issue to those who don't want to be a part of it.
title: SDK Limitation Removal & Options for viewing Massive Avatars
